lessons.title: Python Fundamentals
lessons.summary: Understand python fundamentals by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Data structures
paragraphs: List: An ordered mutable sequence supports indexing and append.
Tuple: An ordered immutable sequence represents a fixed record.
Dictionary: A mapping associates unique hashable keys with values.
Set: An unordered collection of unique hashable elements supports membership and set operations.

sections.title: Control flow
paragraphs: For loop: Iterates over items supplied by an iterable.
While loop: Repeats while a Boolean condition is true.
Break: Exits the nearest enclosing loop immediately.
Continue: Skips the rest of the current iteration and starts the next one.

sections.title: Functions and scope
paragraphs: Return: Ends a function and supplies a result to its caller.
Parameter: A name in a function definition binds an incoming argument.
Local variable: A name assigned within a function normally belongs to its local scope.
Default argument: A value used when an argument is omitted is evaluated at definition time.

sections.title: Errors and resources
paragraphs: Try/except: Handles an anticipated exception raised by an operation.
Finally: Runs cleanup on normal completion and when an exception leaves the try block.
With statement: Uses a context manager to enter and reliably release a resource.
Raise: Signals an exception explicitly rather than returning a misleading success value.

sections.title: Iteration and copying
paragraphs: Generator: Produces values lazily and may be consumed only once.
List comprehension: Builds a new list by mapping or filtering an iterable.
Shallow copy: Creates a new outer container while retaining references to nested objects.
Deep copy: Recursively copies nested objects subject to their copying behavior.

sections.title: Change definition
paragraphs: Acceptance criterion: A concrete observable behavior defines whether the change succeeds.
Small change: A bounded diff makes review and fault isolation easier.
Repository context: Existing code and conventions constrain a useful generated proposal.
Out-of-scope boundary: Explicit exclusions prevent an assistant from expanding the task unintentionally.

sections.title: Verification tools
paragraphs: Unit test: Checks a bounded behavior with controlled inputs.
Integration test: Checks interactions across real component boundaries.
Type checker: Finds incompatible types without proving runtime correctness.
Manual visual review: Inspects appearance and user interactions that automated checks may miss.

sections.title: Review evidence
paragraphs: Diff inspection: Read the actual changed code and its consequences.
Requirement trace: Compare the final behavior against the requested contract.
Independent check: Use evidence beyond the assistant's claim that its own patch works.
Dependency verification: Confirm a proposed package exists, is appropriate and has acceptable provenance.

sections.title: Safe collaboration
paragraphs: Secret exclusion: Do not place credentials in prompts, generated code or committed examples.
Least privilege: Limit the assistant and generated app to necessary permissions.
Human authorization: A consequential external action requires an authorized decision.
Reversible checkpoint: Keep a recoverable state before accepting a substantial change.

sections.title: Failure recovery
paragraphs: Reproduce: Establish concrete steps and inputs that trigger the defect.
Root-cause analysis: Find the failed assumption rather than patching only the symptom.
Rollback: Restore a known working revision when a change must be removed.
Honest limitation: Report what is not verified rather than claiming unsupported success.

sections.title: Request composition
paragraphs: Messages: Ordered role-labelled content supplies the conversational input.
Model identifier: Selects the documented model to handle a request.
Output limit: Caps allowed generated output according to the API contract.
System instruction: Supplies application-level behavior separately from ordinary user content.

sections.title: Response interpretation
paragraphs: Content block: Contains a piece of response output and has a documented type.
Stop reason: Indicates why generation ended, such as a limit or a tool request.
Usage metadata: Reports measured token consumption for the request.
Request identifier: Correlates a specific API request with logs and provider support.

sections.title: Error handling
paragraphs: Authentication error: Check credential validity and the documented authorization scheme.
Rate limit: Use bounded backoff and observe provider retry guidance.
Malformed request: Correct the payload rather than repeatedly sending the same invalid request.
Transient server failure: Retry only when the operation and retry policy permit it.

sections.title: Streaming
paragraphs: Event parser: Interpret incremental events using their documented framing and types.
Cancellation: Stop an unwanted stream and release associated resources.
Final aggregate: Assemble complete content and metadata before treating partial output as final.
Backpressure: Prevent a slow consumer from accumulating unbounded buffered output.

sections.title: Application boundaries
paragraphs: Backend credential: Keep provider secrets in a trusted server-side environment.
Timeout: Bound how long a call can wait before recovery.
Schema validation: Check response structure before using it in application logic.
Cost accounting: Track actual usage against a configured budget without assuming every request costs the same.

sections.title: HTTP operations
paragraphs: GET: Requests a resource representation and should not perform intended state changes.
POST: Submits data for processing and is not inherently idempotent.
PUT: Replaces a target resource and is defined as idempotent.
DELETE: Requests removal of a target resource and is defined as idempotent despite varying responses.

sections.title: Status categories
paragraphs: 2xx: The HTTP operation was successfully handled, though application data still needs validation.
4xx: The client request cannot be fulfilled as sent.
5xx: The server failed to fulfill an apparently valid request.
3xx: Additional navigation or redirection behavior is indicated.

sections.title: Identity and authority
paragraphs: Authentication: Establishes who a caller is.
Authorization: Determines which actions that identity may perform.
TLS: Protects data in transit and authenticates the server when properly validated.
CORS: Controls browser access to responses across origins; it is not user authorization.

sections.title: Retry correctness
paragraphs: Idempotency key: Deduplicates a logical operation when the server supports that contract.
Backoff with jitter: Spreads bounded retries to reduce synchronized load.
Deadline: Limits the total time spent attempting an operation.
Payload repair: Changes invalid request data rather than retrying it unchanged.

sections.title: Data contracts
paragraphs: Input validation: Check the caller's data before using it.
Response validation: Check received data against the expected client contract.
Version compatibility: Handle API changes explicitly rather than assuming schemas stay identical.
Error recovery state: Show actionable failure without fabricating a success or clearing good data.

sections.title: Tool lifecycle
paragraphs: Tool definition: Describes a callable capability and its argument schema to the model.
Tool request: A model-produced name and arguments request an action; they do not execute it.
Application execution: Trusted application code validates and invokes the selected tool.
Tool result: Returns an observation linked to the originating request for the next model turn.

sections.title: Argument checks
paragraphs: Structural validation: Verify required fields, types and allowed fields.
Semantic validation: Check business constraints such as a positive amount or valid date range.
Authorization check: Ensure the caller is permitted to act on the referenced resource.
Allowlist lookup: Resolve tool names only against explicitly registered capabilities.

sections.title: Side effects
paragraphs: Read-only tool: Retrieves information without intended external state changes.
Confirmation gate: Obtains authorization for a consequential action before execution.
Idempotent execution: Deduplicates repeated logical actions using an explicit contract.
Audit record: Records action identity and outcome without exposing unnecessary secrets.

sections.title: Result handling
paragraphs: Call correlation: Associate each result with its originating tool-call identifier.
Failure result: Report tool failure explicitly rather than fabricating an observation.
Untrusted content: Treat returned documents as data rather than privileged instructions.
Bounded result: Limit returned volume so the next request stays within its context budget.

sections.title: Loop control
paragraphs: Iteration limit: Caps the number of model-tool rounds.
Time budget: Bounds total elapsed execution time.
Cost budget: Bounds accumulated usage or spend.
Final response: Ends the loop when no more tool action is required and supplies the user-facing answer.
